problem: Secure Apple's future and Microsoft's own position.
title: Microsoft invests $150 million in Apple and commits to Office for Mac
context: Apple was struggling and Microsoft's Office was important to Mac users.
decision_made: Invest $150 million in non-voting Apple stock and commit to continuing Office and Internet Explorer for the Mac.
action_taken: Announced at Macworld Boston on 6 August 1997; Apple agreed to bundle Internet Explorer and the companies signed a patent cross-licence.
observed_outcome: Not documented in the sources used. Sources disagree on what happened to the stake later.
lessons: A rival can help a struggling partner when it depends on the partner's platform and wants to ease regulatory pressure.
limitations: Commitment length is reported as five years in some sources. Later handling of the stake is conflicting (a sale for $550 million versus a conversion to common stock) and was not reconciled.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft said it would invest $150 million in non-voting Apple stock and keep developing Office for the Mac.
TidBITS noted the non-voting stock gave Microsoft no control over Apple.
